method: Thesis exposure = sum over open theses of posterior x value-pool weight (mandatory infrastructure 1.0, pricing power / scarce 0.9, abundant -0.3, new risk -0.6, loses pricing power -1.0). Final = exposure x (0.5 + opportunity/100) x (1 + gap/100) x technical readiness (trend template) x attention (not-priced +15%, crowded -20%). 'ready' = passes the book's entry gate today.

picks.why: Highest composite (7.6) with zero headwind: it sits in five theses at once, and the ones doing the work are the high-posterior physical-layer calls — T-004 electrons-before-silicon at 98.3, T-007 format absorption at 94.5, T-006 trade scarcity rents at 88.7. Reality 60 against pricing 43 gives a +17 expectations gap, meaning the market is paying mid-cap-contractor multiples for an asset the theses classify as a crew-owning aggregator of scarce skilled trades with pricing power. Technicals are already stage-2 (88) with no attention flag and no crowding — the tape has moved but the narrative has not, which is the rarest configuration in this set.
picks.entry_condition: Buy now on the stage-2 uptrend; add on any pullback that holds the rising 50-day without breaking stage structure. Confirmation to size up: Q3/Q4 specialty-contractor calls naming craft labour as the binding constraint with extending backlog (the T-006 next-signal).
picks.key_risk: IESC is levered to data-centre and electrification project flow; the T-006 falsifier — trade wage ratio flat and backlogs shortening — would hit it fastest, and a small-cap contractor with no narrative support gets no bid on a single backlog miss.

picks.why: Carries the single largest thesis contribution in the file (2.66 from T-008 global rails at 95.0 posterior) plus T-002 sovereign/on-prem AI at 81.4, and it is scored as mandatory infrastructure for 24/7 compliance and surveillance — a layer that gets paid regardless of which venue wins. Reality 83 is the highest fundamental score in the candidate set and still exceeds pricing 69 for a +15 gap, with attention only 41 and explicitly not crowded. The market is paying for the AI narrative (76) but not for the settlement-infrastructure and fraud-graph roles the theses assign it.
picks.entry_condition: Enter on stage-2 continuation; stage the position rather than taking it whole, given pricing is already 69. Second tranche on the T-008 next-signal — a top-five broker going live with continuously traded tokenised equities with named market makers.
picks.key_risk: Narrative 76 versus pricing 69 means much of the expectations gap is sentiment-dependent; a multiple compression event in high-multiple software would overwhelm the fundamental gap, and T-001 (57.2 posterior) is the weakest leg in its stack.

picks.why: Perfect technical score (100), stage-2, ready, and it is the security name that appears in six theses with five of them at posterior ≥81 — including T-005 at 96.0 and T-004 at 98.3 where it is tagged mandatory_infrastructure rather than discretionary spend. Opportunity 71 is the highest in the file. The honest caveat: expectations gap is only +3 (reality 74 vs pricing 71), so this is a quality-and-momentum expression of the security-as-standing-consumption thesis, not a mispricing.
picks.entry_condition: Buy on the current stage-2 structure, but size smaller than IESC/PLTR because there is no valuation cushion. Re-rate to full size only if the FY enterprise IT print shows security spend >10% while total IT spend grows <2% — the explicit T-002 validation condition.
picks.key_risk: If that same print shows security budgets compressing to 5–7%, T-002 collapses onto a single leg and the whole security complex de-rates; with a +3 gap, FTNT has no margin of safety for that outcome.

picks.why: Highest-conviction thesis stack in the industrial cohort — 6.7 exposure dominated by T-006 (2.39) and T-004 (1.77), with roles in crew-owning field labour, prefab, and power/electrical equipment. Reality 67 versus pricing 55 is a +12 gap and it is explicitly named in the T-006 next-signal as one of the three companies whose call commentary validates or falsifies the trade-scarcity leg. It is a watch, not a buy, purely because technicals are emerging (62) rather than confirmed.
picks.entry_condition: Wait for the stage transition from emerging to confirmed stage-2 uptrend — a decisive breakout on expanding volume. Do not anticipate the base.
picks.key_risk: Same structural exposure as IESC, so buying both concentrates the portfolio in one labour-scarcity bet; if data-centre mechanical backlog decelerates, FIX and IESC correlate to nearly one.

picks.why: The cheapest expression of the physical-layer theses in the file: pricing 41 against reality 47 (+6 gap), with 6.76 thesis exposure led by T-007 at 2.65 and T-006 at 2.39 — repair/renovation pricing power, skilled-trade scarcity, and residential electrification as mandatory infrastructure. No narrative score and no attention score at all, which is why the discount exists — nothing is telling this story.
picks.entry_condition: Strictly conditional: it is basing/downtrend (technical 50). Enter only after a confirmed base breakout with the stage flipping to uptrend. Until then it is a watchlist name, not a position.
picks.key_risk: A basing chart with a modest +6 gap can base for a long time; the absorbed opportunity cost is real, and the thesis stack overlaps heavily with IESC and FIX without offering their technical readiness.

picks.why: The only Financials name that is both technically ready and free of a negative expectations gap. Its T-001 contribution (2.69) is the largest single-thesis weight in the payments cohort, and it holds five distinct T-001 roles — delegated authorization, liability absorption, credential custody, bundled consumer protection, agent-initiated settlement — plus the T-002 fraud-graph scarcity role at 81.4. Attention is only 27, the lowest in the set: nobody is paying for the agentic-commerce optionality.
picks.entry_condition: Buy on the emerging uptrend as a low-beta anchor. Add materially on the T-001 next-signal: a top-three network or top-ten issuer publishing explicit chargeback-parity rules for agent-initiated transactions.
picks.key_risk: T-001 posterior is 57.2 — by far the weakest thesis here — and the +3 gap means the base case is already fairly priced; if agent-initiated commerce routes around card rails to the T-008 tokenised settlement path, Visa is the disintermediated party, not the toll collector.

picks.why: Largest raw thesis exposure in the entire file (6.92), anchored on T-004 at 98.3 posterior contributing 2.75 — power generation scarce, nuclear/SMR supply chain scarce, grid orchestration mandatory. Reality 58 against pricing 50 gives a +8 gap with attention at just 29, the second-lowest here, despite a narrative score of 77 — an unusual combination suggesting the story exists but positioning does not.
picks.entry_condition: Do not buy yet — technical stage is basing_or_downtrend at 50. Require a completed base and stage-2 confirmation, ideally coincident with the T-004 next-signal: a second and third hyperscaler disclosing power- or permit-driven schedule slips.
picks.key_risk: T-004 requires silicon to loosen relative to electrons; if GPU spot rates and memory pricing stay tight, the constraint narrative diffuses and GEV's order book gets re-read as cyclical rather than structural. The weak tape means the market may already be pricing that.

memo.portfolio_note: This list is deliberately two-bodied: a physical-layer cluster (IESC, FIX, EME, GEV) expressing the highest-posterior theses in the file — T-004 at 98.3, T-005-adjacent electrification, T-007 at 94.5, T-006 at 88.7 — and a digital-trust cluster (PLTR, FTNT, V) expressing T-008 at 95.0, T-009 at 91.1 and T-002 at 81.4. The physical cluster is where the expectations gaps actually live (IESC +17, FIX +12, GEV +8, EME +6) and the digital cluster is where the technical readiness lives; only IESC and PLTR have both, which is why they are the core. The obvious concentration risk is that IESC, FIX and EME are near-substitutes — same crew-owning-contractor role, same T-006/T-007 stack — so they should be treated as one position sized across three tickers, not three positions. I excluded PANW (-18), CRWD (-20), NET (-17), ETN (-17) and XYZ (-28) despite strong thesis exposure and perfect technicals: negative expectations gaps mean the theses are already in the price, and buying a correct thesis at a paid-for price is how this framework loses money. What would change the list: a failed T-006 print (flat trade wage ratio plus shortening backlogs) would cut the entire industrial cluster to zero; a T-002 falsification (security spend compressing to 5–7% in a flat IT-spend year) would remove FTNT and make ZS and the rest of the security complex uninvestable here; and a resolved T-001 liability standard would promote Visa from anchor to core position.
